speaker: Doctor
text:
Welcome to my office. I see you have a psychiatric history and a new movement disorder; have you noticed any tremors, stiffness, or involuntary movements, and do they occur at rest or when you are trying to move?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Comprehensive Metabolic Panel, Thyroid Function Tests, Vitamin B12 Level.
REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain with contrast.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: COMPLETE BLOOD COUNT: WBC 5,000/μL, Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 250,000/μL; COMPREHENSIVE METABOLIC PANEL: Sodium 140 mEq/L, Potassium 4.0 mEq/L, Chloride 100 mEq/L, Bicarbonate 24 mEq/L, AST 25 U/L, ALT 20 U/L, Bilirubin 1.0 mg/dL, Alkaline Phosphatase 75 U/L; THYROID FUNCTION TESTS: TSH 2.5 mIU/L, Free T4 1.1 ng/dL. Note: Vitamin B12 Level and MRI Brain with contrast images were not included in the provided data source. NORMAL READINGS.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the normal labs; since we don't have the B12 or MRI results yet, have you recently started any new medications, particularly for your psychiatric condition, or been exposed to toxins like carbon monoxide? Also, does your movement disorder affect one side of your body more than the other, and have you noticed any changes in your vision, speech, or swallowing?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old college student. The patient is here for a follow-up appointment. He was recently diagnosed with schizophrenia and started on risperidone approximately 2 months ago. Reports a significant improvement in psychiatric symptoms since the start of treatment.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Drug-Induced Tardive Dyskinesia secondary to Risperidone. Given your age, recent initiation of risperidone for schizophrenia, and new onset movement disorder with normal metabolic workup, the clinical picture strongly suggests tardive dyskinesia rather than acute dystonia or serotonin syndrome. We will proceed with a detailed observation of your movements and consider switching your antipsychotic to a lower risk agent like clozapine or quetiapine after we confirm the specific choreoathetoid patterns you are experiencing.
